title: Investment Fraud — Guaranteed Returns and Crypto Scams
publisher: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
text: SEBI (Securities and Exchange Board of India) warns investors about fraudulent investment schemes that promise guaranteed high returns. No legitimate investment can guarantee fixed returns higher than bank FD rates (currently ~6–7% per year). Any scheme promising 20%, 40%, or 100% guaranteed returns is fraudulent. Common investment fraud types in India: (1) Ponzi/MLM schemes — early investors are paid using money from new investors; eventually collapses. (2) Fake crypto or forex trading platforms — promise huge profits, but withdrawals are blocked or funds disappear. (3) WhatsApp/Telegram 'stock tips' groups — 'insider information' that is actually pump-and-dump manipulation. (4) Chit fund fraud — unregistered chit funds that collect money and disappear. (5) Government-endorsed crypto — no cryptocurrency has Indian government endorsement; PM Modi has not endorsed any crypto scheme. Red flags: (1) 'Guaranteed returns' with no risk. (2) 'Refer friends and earn commission' (pyramid structure). (3) Pressure to invest immediately before the scheme closes. (4) Unregistered entity — verify at SEBI's website (sebi.gov.in) or RBI's list of registered entities. Never invest money you cannot afford to lose, especially in unverified schemes. Report investment fraud at sebi.gov.in or cybercrime.gov.in.
